What the Outer Criterion Can Resolve at This Fit

Source: R/outer_context.R
criterion_resolution.Rd

Computes the size of a difference in the criterion that carries no information, from the fit at the point.

Usage

criterion_resolution(st, spec, design, method, criterion_at)

Arguments

st

An evaluation's stored state, carrying ok, par, split, score, cf, hy, ctx and value.

spec

The specification.

design

The design.

method

An OuterMethod().

criterion_at

A function of (cf, hy, par, ctx) returning what the search is running, a prediction-error criterion or a marginal one. It is passed in and not chosen here, because the marginal criterion of a fit whose search runs aic() is a quantity that the search does not evaluate.

Value

A single positive number, or NA_real_ where the pieces are not available. Where the mode error exceeds mode_error_limit(), the NA carries the attribute mode_error, which holds that error.

Details

The criterion is read at the penalized mode, and the inner fit stops short of that mode by whatever its rule allows. Writing \(g\) for the score at which the inner fit stopped and \(K = H + S\) for the penalized information, the mode is out by \(\delta\beta = K^{-1} g\), and the criterion read at \(\hat\beta - \delta\beta\) instead of at \(\hat\beta\) differs by an amount that equals the difference between two evaluations from different warm starts. One assembly of the criterion at given coefficients gives it, with no refit.

The criterion carries \(-\tfrac{1}{2}\log\lvert K(\beta)\rvert\), which is not stationary in \(\beta\), so a mode error enters it at first order and the quadratic form \(\tfrac{1}{2} g' K^{-1} g\) does not bound the change by itself. The criterion is therefore evaluated at the displaced coefficients.

The reading estimates the spread of the criterion across warm starts. It is usually below that spread, because the spread is a range over several paths and the reading is one deviation. A resolution smaller than the true one leaves the search where it was, and a larger one stops a search before it has converged.

The reading is NA where \(g' K^{-1} g / 2\) exceeds mode_error_limit(), because a displacement computed from an inner fit that is far from its mode is not a resolution.

See also

outer_fit(), optimizers7::armijo()
